sections.lead: Sinnix is the NixOS configuration for a personal computing estate — one workstation, one cloud replica, one router — with three ambitions: total declarativity (undeclared state does not survive a reboot), continuous self-observation (capture services feeding a personal data lake), and agent operability (AI agents co-maintain the system). This atlas is emitted by a program: volatile figures are probed at generation time, findings are predicates that disappear when no longer true, and --verify re-probes a published copy against reality. Prose sections are deliberately data-free framing — the provenance table at the end says which is which.
sections.vocabulary:
Orientation and vocabulary

Every term of art is defined before use; later sections rely on these.

Nix and NixOS terms

flake
A Nix repository format with pinned external dependencies (inputs) recorded in a lock file; builds are reproducible from the repository alone.
module
A Nix file contributing options and configuration; NixOS merges hundreds of them into one machine description.
derivation
One buildable unit (a package, a test, a script) — Nix's unit of work.
generation
One complete, immutable build of the operating system; activation is atomic and old generations stay bootable.
switch / boot
Applying a generation to the running machine immediately, vs. only making it the default for the next restart.
Home Manager
Declarative management of the user's home directory (dotfiles, user services); abbreviated HM.
overlay
A local modification layer over the upstream package set — a patch, build-flag change, or dependency swap carried here rather than upstream.
devshell
The project shell environment providing the repo's commands (switch, boot, check, update…), entered via direnv.

Estate terms

surface
The estate's registration record for one runtime thing it owns — usually a systemd unit, sometimes a data path or a dynamic unit family. Declares manager, resource class, observability, and captured outputs; all surfaces serialize into one inventory file (§10).
resource class
A named bundle of scheduling/memory policy a surface inherits (§9).
command class
The same idea for commands: a launcher places a command into the slice and policy matching its class.
slice
systemd's resource-control grouping; the estate gives slices explicit CPU/IO weights and memory budgets.
capture lane
One continuous local data-collection service writing to the data lake; lanes share the envelope record format (§11).
sentinel
The freshness watchdog flagging capture lanes whose output has gone stale.
bead
A work item in the repo's issue tracker (bd); ids look like sinnix-a1dp. Beads are the durable memory for decisions and incidents; cited throughout.
agent lane
A preconfigured launcher for an AI coding agent — vendor CLI × tool-server profile × model backend.
MCP
Model Context Protocol — how agent CLIs attach external tool servers; the estate keeps one registry with per-agent profiles.
data lake
/realm/data/ — canonical personal data: captures, exports, libraries, derived products, knowledge vault.
zram
A compressed block device in RAM used as first-priority swap: evicted pages compress into memory instead of hitting disk.
sections.deployment:
Anatomy of a deployment

What actually happens when the operator (or an agent) types switch — every stage exists because its absence once shipped a failure:

#StageWhat and why
1resolveFind the live git checkout (never a store copy — a store copy has no git metadata and would stamp the generation "revision unknown", blinding the drift tripwire in stage 7).
2lockTake /tmp/sinnix-switch.lock. NixOS itself has no guard against two concurrent activations interleaving service restarts; since today, a second activation queues rather than aborts (aborts produced silent no-op deployments).
3preflightsinnix-preflight switch: read-only checks — memory headroom, disk, no concurrent generation operation, live agent-job count. Blockers exit non-zero; a documented one-shot override exists for deliberate exceptions.
4containThe build runs inside nix-build.slice via a transient systemd unit: idle CPU/IO scheduling, the 22/28 GB memory budget — a rebuild cannot starve the desktop.
5build + activatenh (a nixos-rebuild frontend) evaluates the flake (a multi-GB, single-threaded interpretation of the whole configuration), builds derivations (now up to 4 in parallel), registers the generation, and runs activation. A fallback path can activate the exact built system if the frontend fails after building.
6cache-pushOn success, the sinex closure is published to the personal binary cache in the background, so the replica and reinstalls substitute instead of recompiling.
7drift stampThe generation carries the exact repo commit; nixos-version --configuration-revision answers "is the running system this code?" — used repeatedly today to catch half-applied states.

boot shares every stage but defers activation to the next restart — chosen today for the D-Bus implementation swap, which cannot be applied under a running session.

The input signal chain

Physical input passes through userspace pipelines before the compositor sees it — the estate's keystroke capture and key remapping happen here, not in the desktop:

Hetzner AX42, headless profile: runs the event-capture platform in replica role (database + queue for remote thin clients, no local capture). Bootstrap by installer, steady state by fleet deploy.

OpenWrt, entirely generated from Nix and pushed over SSH with a backup → package sync → configuration → health-check sequence — a managed host without being a NixOS host.
sections.secrets:
Secrets

33 encrypted secrets measured live outside the repository (/realm/data/secrets/sinnix/secret/*.age, age-encrypted to host and operator keys). The secrets module auto-discovers the directory: each file becomes a decrypted runtime path under /run/agenix/ (owner-readable only — 33 present live, visible to root) plus, for non-password material, a shell environment export. Decryption keys point directly at /persist so secrets decrypt before the impermanence bind-mounts assemble the home directory. Because the store lives outside the flake, evaluation must be told the path explicitly — pure evaluation would silently see an empty secrets set, a failure shape the deployment commands guard against by design.
sections.capture:
The capture machinery

The estate's most distinctive programme: continuous local recording of the operator's digital environment, on the doctrine capture first, enrich later. Every lane writes the shared envelope:

Lane-by-lane live status is folded into the inventory table (§10); the day's capture headlines:

  • The replay ring recorded its first frame ever today. Root cause of its lifetime of failure: the unit's own mount-namespace sandboxing. An unprivileged user manager can only create a mount namespace by first unsharing a user namespace — inside which the kernel-capture helper's granted capability is namespace-relative, while the kernel checks the framebuffer ioctl against the initial namespace. Sandboxing this unit and capturing the screen are mutually exclusive; the sandboxing lost, a start-limit now prevents silent crash-looping, and a real 4K clip was saved through the production hotkey path.
  • Screen stills remain HDR-degraded (black frames via the standard capture path) — compositor/driver-level, tracked, distinct from the replay mechanism which reads the display controller directly and demonstrably works with HDR on.
  • The observer has a blind spot: today's controlled experiment exposed that the live-state prober omits two active capture services from its unit view — both blinded research arms independently "discovered" a phantom outage. Filed as sinnix-gcuv.
  • The primary-selection lane landed, with an empirically-derived debounce: one selection gesture fires the watcher up to 7 times in 40 ms.
sections.agents:
Agent tooling

Lanes and profiles

Launchers form a matrix: vendor CLI × tool-server profile × model backend, all rendered from one data table. The measured profile compositions measured (computed from the registry's own selection function):

ProfileTool servers attachedIntent
leangithub · context7 · polylogue · sinexdefault coding sessions — fast startup, core context
evidence+ lynchpinhistorical reconstruction work
full+ serena (code-index)heavy engineering sessions
browserfull + three Chrome-control variantsweb automation (live profile, agent-private, private-visible)
orchestratecore + agent-controlfleet coordination

Alternate backends per lane: subscription cloud (default), an alternative API vendor, or local models via the translation gateway — plus a contributor-tier lane whose provider may train on its traffic, flagged so confidential material stays off it.

Guard rails

  • Model discipline — dispatching a subagent without an explicit model choice is hard-denied by hook.
  • Shell policy — dangerous command shapes (force-pushes to the published branch, tracker anti-patterns) are blocked pre-execution.
  • Dispatch ledger + vacuity sampling — every dispatch is logged; suspiciously fast, citation-free successes get sampled for headless judging.
  • Attested job control — headless jobs carry manifests binding PID + process-start-time + control-group, so PID reuse can never impersonate a live job; consumed by the prober, the pre-reboot check, and orphan classification.

Today's addition: the clean-room technique

The controlled experiment needed workers with zero ambient context (no injected history, no personal steering state, no memory). Solution, now reusable: point the CLI at a fresh configuration directory containing only credentials. Verified to produce workers that know nothing but their prompt — the difference matters, because a session-start context injection would have leaked the answers to the very questions the experiment asked.
sections.pilot:
A long-parked, pre-registered A/B: does a coordinated two-researcher team (one exchange of notes, then a synthesizer) beat three independent researchers plus a mechanical-style coordinator, on a fixed estate-analysis question? Method: sealed answer key written before launch (hashes recorded), clean-room workers, blinded scoring by a stronger model against the key, arm identities and costs unsealed only after scores locked.

quality (weighted 0–4)notional costwall-clockcoordination msgs
teams (2+synth)3.45$4.688.8 min2
independent (3+coord)2.73$4.4210.4 min0

Verdict: adopt (qualified) — the quality margin was nearly twice the pre-registered threshold, at cost parity within 6% and faster wall-clock. The separator was error load, not brilliance: the independent arm shipped one confident verified error and explicitly argued down the hypothesis that turned out true (the observer blind spot), while the team's coordination round distributed verification. Both arms independently confirmed the (operator-known) event-platform outage; both missed the same subtle defect class (a live service missing from the registry) — evidence that inverse drift is the hardest kind to see. Full protocol + results: docs/agent-teams-pilot.json.
sections.architecture_head:
Repository and evaluation architecture

Evaluation follows one pipeline: flake.nix pins 22 inputs and hands each host to mkHost (flake/nixos.nix), which builds a shared context — module factories, pure data tables (the MCP registry, runtime policy, the local-model roster, the agent-lane matrix), and the helper library lib.sinnix — injected into every module. modules/default.nix auto-imports the whole tree; a new module needs zero wiring.

The input constellation

The 22 inputs measured divide into four families, and the two deliberate exceptions to normal pinning are the interesting part:

FamilyInputsPinning story
package setsnixpkgs, nixpkgs-ai Exception 1: nixpkgs-ai is a second, unfollowed nixpkgs pin feeding only the CUDA-narrowed AI packages. Routine update excludes it, because any movement invalidates GPU-library builds that take hours to recompile; it is bumped only by explicit choice.
own projectssinex, polylogue, lynchpin, scribe-tap, intercept-bounce, yt-polisher, noctalia, beads Exception 2: sinex does not follow the main nixpkgs, so its build hash survives nixpkgs bumps — each revision compiles at most once, then the binary cache serves it (the desktop publishes the built closure back to the cache after every successful switch). lynchpin is a local-path input; the rest come from their public repos so deployment never consumes local checkout state.
NixOS machineryhome-manager, impermanence, agenix, disko, lanzaboote, colmena, nixos-anywhere, flake-parts, treefmt-nix ordinary follows-nixpkgs pins: home management, ephemeral root, secrets, disk layout, secure boot, fleet deploy, bootstrap installs, flake structure, formatting
desktop extrasstylix, nix-vscode-extensions, flake-utils-for-colmena theming and editor-extension supply
sections.architecture_tail:
Module taxonomy and factory contracts

If the thing is…It lives inCount
system infrastructure — networking, storage, the build daemon's own policy, secrets, persistence, the runtime registrymodules/*.nix16
a user-facing capabilitymodules/features/{cli,desktop,dev,system}/48
a long-running daemonmodules/services/83
a deployment-class default (headless cloud, desktop)modules/profiles/3
a reusable helpermodules/lib/5

Two contracts give the tree its character: features are default-ON (everything under features/ is part of a host's identity; hosts express exceptions), and services are default-OFF (hosts opt in; a service declares its surface in the same breath as its unit, so governance is co-located with the thing governed).

Standing rules

  • No compatibility aliases — renames update every reference in one pass; git history is the archive.
  • Comments carry live constraints only — stories live in commit messages and beads, reachable via git blame (enforced repo-wide today).
  • The repository is public — machine config and ordinary identity are intentional content; secrets and private data are excluded by review; only master is published.
  • Tests protect contracts, never restate configuration — §15.
sections.governance_head:
Runtime governance

Modules declare surfaces → surfaces name resource classes → classes map to systemd policy and slices → everything serializes to /etc/sinnix/runtime-inventory.json, consumed by the placement launcher, the observability prober, and machine telemetry. Policy source of truth: flake/data/runtime-defaults.nix.
sections.governance_tail:
Today's overhaul: retiring serialize-everything

Until this morning a host-wide single-holder lock (the heavy-work lease) serialized all build and test work. Audited against its own telemetry today, it was removed outright: 1,246 refusals in one 13.5-hour window against a median hold of 13 secondsmeasured, while memory never approached danger and stall windows kept happening anyway. Follow-up forensics reattributed the real pressure: at the worst recorded moment the agent slice held 21.5 GB RAM + 19.4 GB swap — not conversations, but 57 concurrent C++ compiler processes spawned by an agent-invoked Python environment build inside the agent slice, plus a misplaced inference server. The tuning programme (sinnix-a1dp, P1) closes the routing escape and derives budgets from measurement; Nix build parallelism rose from 1 job to 4 under the existing ceilings; every surviving lock queues instead of aborting.
sections.storage_doctrine:
The wear doctrine

The root SATA drive has a finite write budget, so every write-heavy workload is routed elsewhere: build scratch to a copy-on-write-exempt cache on root, repository scratch and agent working copies to the NVMe, databases to copy-on-write-exempt subvolumes, the journal to the NVMe. Adding a write-heavy path to root is a reviewed decision.

Impermanence

The workstation's root is rebuilt every boot. State survives only through explicit declarations co-located with the owning module — 21 persistence declarations across 14 modulesmeasured — collected centrally and bind-mounted from /persist. The system cannot silently accrete undocumented state, because undocumented state does not survive the night.

Backup chain

btrfs snapshots (producer) → hourly Borg drain to the backup HDD, under the durability gate: a snapshot is deleted only after the drain proves a matching archive exists. Status is an append-only capture stream; a periodic restore drill proves archives are readable. All copies share one building — off-site storage was retired by the operator and its return is an accepted open question.inferred
sections.ai_head:
The local AI platform

A tiered stack of self-hosted model servers, all loopback-bound, all on-demand: each heavyweight server sits behind a tiny socket-activation proxy that owns the public port; the first connection starts the backend, and 30 idle seconds later the proxy's exit tears the backend down, releasing RAM/VRAM. The two GPU inference hubs declare mutual exclusion — starting one stops the other, because both want the whole 3080.

sections.runbook:
Operator runbook

Task-oriented recipes; every command is the estate's own front door, not a raw tool. Read-only unless a task says otherwise.

TaskHow
apply configuration nowswitch (devshell) or cd /realm/project/sinnix && nix develop --command switch. Never raw nh os switch — the wrapper owns containment, lock, preflight, cache-push.
apply on next rebootboot — used when live activation would disrupt (bus swaps, session-critical units).
rehearse risky changetest-vm boots the built system in QEMU first.
routine dependency updateupdate — bumps every input except the CUDA-pinned one; that one only via update nixpkgs-ai (hours of GPU recompiles otherwise).
run the test tierscheck (default tier, CI-equivalent) · check-all (adds VM boots + host builds) · smoke (live probes).
is the running system this code?nixos-version --configuration-revision vs git rev-parse HEAD — the drift tripwire; a -dirty suffix means uncommitted tree state was built in.
add a background servicenew file in modules/services/ using the service factory (name, surface, options, config) — zero central wiring; enable it in hosts/sinnix-prime/default.nix; declare persistence in the same change; switch; confirm its surface appears in this atlas's inventory.
add a capture lanesame as a service, plus: write through the envelope library, register the capture output with a cadence or staleness budget so the sentinel watches it, and land a contract test.
edit a secretagenix (devshell) — operates on the out-of-repo secret store; a rebuilt system picks up the new material at /run/agenix/.
regenerate this atlassinnix estate-report; check a stale copy with sinnix estate-report --verify.
recover from a bad activationprevious generations remain bootable: pick one in the boot menu, or sudo nix-env --profile /nix/var/nix/profiles/system --rollback then activate. The pre-wipe snapshot taken at each boot covers root-filesystem mistakes.
deploy the replica / routernix run .#deploy-ethereal (bootstrap) / colmena for steady state · nix run .#router-deploy.
see the whole command surfacesinnix help — every packaged script, generated, zero-wiring.
sections.failures:
Failure-pattern catalog

The estate's hardest-won knowledge: recurring failure shapes, each with its tell and its structural fix. Most earned their entry on 2026-08-12 alone.

PatternShapeTripwire / fix
silent no-op deploya lock aborts a background switch; the exit code gets masked; everyone believes the deploy happenedlocks now queue instead of aborting; the drift tripwire catches survivors
quarantined-red testa check lives in a tier nothing executes; it breaks and stays broken for its whole lifetiers must be honestly named; anything fast runs in the default tier (two lifetime-broken fixtures found this way)
fixture that cannot faila test's fake tools are shadowed — generated scripts bake their real tool paths into PATH, and the build sandbox has no /usr/bin/env for the fakes' shebangsrun a copy with the baked PATH line stripped (assert exactly one), patchShebangs the fakes; always ask "what change would make this fail?"
fossil assertiona test restates a config literal or freezes a past decision; every legitimate change breaks it, so it trains people to update tests mechanicallyderive expectations from the source registry, or delete; config content is not contract
silently decaying workaroundan override whose recheck condition can never fail loudly (doCheck=false, disabled test names pytest never validates) outlives its reasonprefer self-verifying spellings (--replace-fail); audit found 9 of 10 recheck conditions had fired unnoticed
capability demoted by sandboxa user unit with any mount-namespace directive silently gets a child user namespace; file capabilities become namespace-relative and kernel checks against the initial namespace failscreen-capture units carry no mount sandboxing — the two are mutually exclusive; a start-limit stops the crash-loop symptom from running for hours
containment escape by indirectioncommand-name routing puts cargo/pytest in the build slice, but an agent-invoked environment builder spawns compilers inside the agent slice57 concurrent C++ compiles in the agent slice, 41 GB footprint; fix track is routing children of build-ish tools to the build slice (tuning programme)
observer blind spotthe live-state prober omits some real units; consumers "discover" phantom outagesboth blinded experiment arms independently hit it; check that every active owned unit appears in the observer's view
generalized-label policya rule justified for workload class A gets applied to class B because both are labeled "heavy"the heavy-work lease: incident-justified for GPU-library compiles, silently serialized 13-second test runs; audit the readers of a policy, not its label
guessed timestampa generated document carries a narrative time instead of a clock reading; the page displays "22m ahead" to anyone who opens ittimestamps only from date -u at write time — this generator does so structurally
eval-breaking metadataa script header references a dependency the packager cannot resolve; every deployment fails at evaluation, silently blocking all other workthe header contract fails loudly at eval — good — but master stayed broken for hours because nothing built between commits; CI on push is the missing tripwire
sections.why:
The why-layer

Every load-bearing mechanism annotated with the incident or decision that birthed it — the estate as explicit scar tissue. Stories live in beads and commit messages; this table is the index, not the archive.

MechanismBorn from
ephemeral root + declared persistencethe decision that undocumented state is a bug class, not a convenience — anything unlisted vanishes at boot, so the config cannot quietly diverge from reality
wear doctrine (nothing write-heavy on root)the root SSD's measured write budget; databases once wrote terabytes/day to it before being moved to copy-on-write-exempt NVMe subvolumes
single-job Nix builds → 4-job with slice ceilings2026-07-06: two concurrent GPU-library compiles exceeded RAM and the early killer took out the compiler; serialization was the first fix, cgroup ceilings the correct one (2026-08-12)

the CUDA-pinned second package seta routine dependency bump once invalidated every GPU library at ~2h rebuild; now those move only by explicit choice
event-platform input not following nixpkgscompile-once economics: each of its revisions builds one time, then every host substitutes from the cache
journal on NVMe, 64 GB / 365 daysmemory-kill forensics needed history the old 2-week wear-limited journal couldn't hold
per-scope agent memory caps, uncapped slice2026-06-18: a shared agent ceiling froze every healthy agent behind one busy one
single earlyoom protect-lista hand-copied second list silently diverged and dropped two session-recovery processes from protection (found 2026-08-12)
capture envelope + capture-first doctrineraw streams are replayable forever; interpretation can be rerun — so capture never waits on enrichment design
attested agent jobs (PID + start-time + cgroup)PID reuse once made a dead job look alive; identity now survives recycling
explicit-model dispatch hookinherited model defaults caused silent cost/quality drift across the agent fleet
drift tripwire (revision-stamped generations)half-applied states: "the config says X" proved nothing about the running machine until the stamp existed

sections.scripts:
Scripts and the command surface

79 scripts, auto-packaged via a mandatory machine-readable header (description + runtime dependencies — a missing header fails evaluation), fronted by a generated meta-command (sinnix help / sinnix <name>). Families: desktop control for agents (window/keyboard/screenshot/browser/terminal), resource placement, the observability prober, the freshness watchdog, pre-flight safety checks, capture workers, backup drills, and operator utilities.
sections.verification:
Verification

Three tiers: 49 default checks (every check run and CI), 5 genuinely heavy ones (3 VM boots + both host builds), and live smoke probes. Today's full-suite audit enforced the standing taxonomy — a test earns its place by protecting behavior, a contract, or an invariant, and is deleted if it restates configuration, freezes a dead decision, asserts formatter-owned text shape, or cannot fail where it runs. The audit found the quarantine tier itself was the biggest defect: nine mislabeled fast checks lived in a tier nothing executed, and two had been silently broken their whole lives. All nine now run everywhere; the broken pair were repaired, one by deriving its expectations from the registry it checks so drift can never fossilize again; two well-written but never-wired tests were completed rather than deleted.
sections.oom_ladder: The out-of-memory ladder: per-scope caps first (a runaway agent tool sacrifices only its own scope), then pressure-scoped kills on the sacrificial build slices, then — journal-verified thresholds measured — a userspace early killer at 3% available memory + 50% swap free (SIGTERM) and 1.5%/25% (SIGKILL), whose protect-list covers only session-recovery processes and is, as of today, derived from a single audited list.
sections.governance_serialized:
What remains serialized (and why)

Exactly one lock survives the retirement of serialize-everything: two concurrent activations (applying a new generation) queue behind each other, because NixOS itself provides no guard against two activation processes interleaving service restarts — each diffs units against a running state the other is mutating. This is a correctness lock, not a resource one, and since 2026-08-12 it queues rather than aborts, because abort-on-contention produced silent no-op deployments.
sections.chronicle:
Session chronicles

Dated entries, one per consequential working session — the atlas's own history, accumulating. The commits-by-hour chart is generated for the current day only.

sections.risks:
Risk register

Durable, non-momentary risks (entered 2026-08-12; momentary conditions belong to the findings predicates, which self-clear):

  • Live memory posture: compressed swap was 98% full at snapshot (11.8/12 GB) with the disk swapfile barely touched — consistent with the reattributed pressure findings, and exactly what the tuning programme exists to fix.
  • HDR still-capture remains broken at the compositor/driver layer.
  • Storage runway: backups at 89%, bulk media at 95%; the capture roadmap already schedules a disk purchase before its next phase. All backups are one-building.
  • D-Bus swap validation waits for the next reboot.
  • Two-session co-evolution worked today via worktree-and-merge discipline plus the tracker as shared state — but it is convention, not mechanism.
sections.method:
Method notes

Queried, not recalled: repository counts from git/ls; inventory and policy from the live inventory JSON; unit states from systemctl per surface; storage from df/du; ports from ss; swap from swapon; pressure history from SQL over the telemetry database; secrets counted in both their encrypted and decrypted locations; profile compositions computed by evaluating the registry's own selection function; experiment figures from its receipts. Holes shown rather than papered over: per-lane daily record counts were not measured (day-file layouts differ per lane), and two backup-posture sentences are tagged inferred. Known drift vector: the concurrent repair session — every figure carries its measurement moment. The three file-preview popups were generated from file contents at publication time; regenerate with the report-tooling's embed script after edits.
